existing_sources_preserved.citation: Anthony D. Smith and Ernest Gellner, Warwick debate, 24 October 1995; published in Nations and Nationalism (1996).

verification.note: Primary Smith opening read on the LSE resource page; Gellner’s reply at https://www.lse.ac.uk/researchAndExpertise/units/gellner/Warwick2.html consulted for cultural continuity and modern mobility/literate culture. The linked introduction dates the event to 1995, distinct from publication. Smith credits Gellner’s teaching but disputes sufficiency of modernist explanation; neither position is a consensus. Gellner’s provocative primordialist label does not define Smith’s own qualified ethno-symbolic position.

relations.relationship: Uses ethnic ties, myths, memories and symbols to investigate the content and appeal of particular nationalisms.
relations.evidence_note: Primary Smith opening, definitions and ethno-symbolic sections; reuses earlier qualified review, with opening/central paragraphs freshly read. He acknowledges most nations’ modernity and does not require a definite prior ethnic community in every case.

relations.relationship: Challenges the sufficiency of Gellner’s general modernist explanation for historically specific national attachments while acknowledging his intellectual contribution.
relations.evidence_note: Directly named Warwick opening: critique of explanatory scope rather than denial of all modern conditions. Smith describes an approach/perspective and limits theoretical certainty; no unchanging ethnic essence or field consensus. Gellner’s reply remains separate.
